Simple Rules for a Simple Type System (mi'e la Ctefà'o)

Keep in mind that all of this is very important to fixing how pro-bridi works, which is crucial for sanitizing xoi/soi.

1. All bridi always have a type. A bridi type is permanent and does neither change nor disappear through pro-bridi instantation or macro* expansion.

2. There exists a default bridi type even when one is not explicitly specified. This type is "su'u". {.i broda} and {.i su'u broda [kei]) are equivalent*.
   - Equuivalent except that if we put the "kei" in there we can refer to everything inside the expression.
        - And yes, if we do that we make a selbri out of the expression (becoming {lo su'u broda} if we "sumtify" it), that we can use to include everything inside it.
          - And yes you could do {.i su'u su'u broda [kei] [kei]}, or put a hundred su'u after each other, but you don't have to do that! "su'u" is not a macro you can expand! Only use as many "su'u"/NU as you need!
     - Consider su'u more as "expression" than "abstraction". Main difference between "su'u" and "du'u" is that "du'u" excludes any other NU while "su'u" does not. See below.

3. Bridi type "inherits" through pro-bridi. Any relevant NU are considered to be contained in the pro-bridi "instantation" ("lo no'a" is all we need, as the type will follow with the no'a).
     - This is *important* because the adverbial clauses need to get the right NU-bridi-type from the "no'a" to refer to the same expression!

<nowiki>*</nowiki> Putting something in a "su'u" does not affect assertion in any way. Assertion is NA, not NU.
    (Not even da'i affects assertion, you simply assert something in an imaginary context)
<nowiki>**</nowiki> I think of any Lojban construct (lo-ku, noi-ku'o, na-ku) as a macro.


As for the main difference among the NU:
"su'u" is all-inclusive and may be any of the other NU.
"non-su'u" (like "du'u") are all-exclusive and exclude any other NU than themselves.


The NU-x2 places are not (yet) covered by this idea.


That's it! Grammar completely supports it! Enjoy your NUs!
